policy.rule: A blocking external assumption must be proven by an executable repository artifact before public API depends on it.

assumptions.claim: DSH Agent creation preserves the caller-bound Principal-derived context as ownerCtx.
Agent setup runs before Session/Agent publication, so pre-publication composition can fail without exposing a partial Agent.
A derived child fiber is lifetime-owned by its parent fiber and parent disposal waits for child cleanup.
ctx.inject is dependency-reactive: losing and restoring a required service unloads and may re-run the injected callback.
Runtime capability providers preserve Tenant/Principal isolation, descendant inheritance, teardown and unpublished setup semantics.

A Principal-owned non-reactive Operation captures required Cordis capabilities exactly once before execute; provider churn cannot re-enter semantic work, and DSH create/resume/failure preserve the Operation/Principal caller boundary.

Pinned DSH Agent scopes share the application Cordis root while ToolRuntime registrations remain scope-aware, and the official dsh-mcp-client reserves serverName root-wide; M5 therefore needs a deterministic per-Principal-Session physical namespace for concurrent Agent-local MCP instances.
